paper.title: Magnetic knot cascade via the stepwise reconnection of helical flux tubes

sources.version: Published version; title, authors, DOI and journal checked on first page

text_evidence_sources: Main-paper and appendix equations and captions

claims.claim: Representative closed field lines progress through trefoil, cinquefoil and septafoil examples.
claims.boundary: Artificial closure and representative instantaneous lines, not unique tracked line identities.

claims.claim: Sampled knot-type distributions shift toward higher crossing numbers.
claims.boundary: 3700 samples per time in a restricted plane; unknotted and 12.5% complex late samples omitted.

claims.claim: Lorentz feedback rotates and stretches lines to enable repeated encounters.
claims.boundary: No isolated force-removal ablation; eventual stretching also ends cascade.

claims.claim: MSF tangency error is below 1% and lower than strength-isosurface error.
claims.boundary: Tangency does not establish temporal uniqueness or classification convergence.

claims.claim: Weak twist, weak magnetic interaction and some profiles do not knot.
claims.boundary: Limited parameter samples; field profile and energy vary together.

source_conflicts: Conclusion prints nc=5 at t=2.25; Figure 15 and §3.4 specify nc=7.
Conclusion inner/outer MSF interval wording conflicts with §3.3; main definitions used.
